title: Ensure password history remember is configured
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 5.3.3.3.1: Ensure password history remember is configured

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: password_history_remember
parameters.description: Minimum number of password history entries to remember (CIS requires 24 or more)

steps.name: Check if the /etc/security/pwhistory.conf file exists
steps.function: 1. Check if the /etc/security/pwhistory.conf file exists using command: `test -f /etc/security/pwhistory.conf`. Expected result: exit status 0 (file exists).

steps.name: Check if the pam_pwhistory module is configured in /etc/pam.d/password-auth or /etc/pam.d/system-auth
steps.function: 2. Check if the pam_pwhistory module is configured in /etc/pam.d/password-auth or /etc/pam.d/system-auth using command: `grep -Pi -- '^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwhistory\.so' /etc/pam.d/password-auth /etc/pam.d/system-auth`. Expected result: at least one match is returned (module is present).

steps.name: Check that the remember option in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf is set to the required value or more
steps.function: 3. Check that the remember option in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf is set to {{ password_history_remember }} or more using command: `grep -Pi -- '^\h*remember\h*=\h*([2-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2,})\b' /etc/security/pwhistory.conf` and verify the value is >= {{ password_history_remember }}. Expected result: a line matching the pattern is returned with a value >= {{ password_history_remember }}.

steps.name: Check that the remember option in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf is not set to less than the required value
steps.function: 4. Check that the remember option in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf is not set to less than {{ password_history_remember }} using command: `grep -Pi -- '^\h*remember\h*=\h*([0-9]|[1-9][0-9])\b' /etc/security/pwhistory.conf` and verify no value is < {{ password_history_remember }}. Expected result: no output (nothing returned).

steps.name: Check that the remember option on the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/password-auth is not set to less than the required value
steps.function: 5. Check that the remember option on the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/password-auth is not set to less than {{ password_history_remember }} using command: `grep -Pi -- '^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwhistory\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?remember=([0-9]|[1-9][0-9])\b' /etc/pam.d/password-auth` and verify no value is < {{ password_history_remember }}. Expected result: no output (nothing returned).

steps.name: Check that the remember option on the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/system-auth is not set to less than the required value
steps.function: 6. Check that the remember option on the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/system-auth is not set to less than {{ password_history_remember }} using command: `grep -Pi -- '^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwhistory\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?remember=([0-9]|[1-9][0-9])\b' /etc/pam.d/system-auth` and verify no value is < {{ password_history_remember }}. Expected result: no output (nothing returned).

steps.name: Check overall compliance status: if /etc/security/pwhistory.conf does not exist, or pam_pwhistory module is not present…
steps.function: 7. Check overall compliance status: if /etc/security/pwhistory.conf does not exist, or pam_pwhistory module is not present in both /etc/pam.d/password-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-auth, then SKIP; otherwise, if all previous checks pass, then PASS; if any check fails, then FAIL. Expected result: PASS if all checks pass, SKIP if prerequisite not met, FAIL if feature exists but is misconfigured.

steps.name: Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance…
steps.function: 8. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

steps.name: Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg with EXACTLY this format:
steps.function:
9. Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg with EXACTLY this format:
AUDIT REPORT — CIS 5.3.3.3.1
Reference: CIS Benchmark checkpoint 5.3.3.3.1
Then for each requirement: REQUIREMENT NN - {{ req_NN }}:
  With fields: Task, Command, Exit code, Data, Status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR), Details.
End with OVERALL COMPLIANCE: section containing Result: {{{ cis_result }}}

steps.function: Output the overall compliance status to the caller.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
reference_procedure:
Run the following command and verify that the remember option is set to 24 or more and meets local site policy in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf:
# grep -Pi -- '^\h*remember\h*=\h*(2[4-9]|[3-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2,})\b'
/etc/security/pwhistory.conf

remember = 24
Run the following command to verify that the remember option is not set to less than 24 on the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/password-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-auth:
# grep -Pi --
'^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwhistory\.so\h+([^#\n\ r]+\h+)?remember=(2[0-3]|1[0-9]|[0-9])\b' /etc/pam.d/system-auth
/etc/pam.d/password-auth

Nothing should be returned
